title: Being affine descends along fpqc coverings (Stacks 02L5)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For $i\in I$ let $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ be the base change of $f$ along $g_i$, the second projection of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f_i$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] for every $i\in I$, then $f$ is affine.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L5 (lemma-descending-property-affine, line 5926: 'The property P(f) = "f is affine" is fpqc local on the base'), the direction 'each base change $X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ has the property $\Rightarrow$ $f$ has it' of Definition Tag 02KO (definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310); proof lines 5931-5965 (via Lemmas Tag 02KP, 02KQ, 02KU, 02L4 and flat base change)

proof.text: *Being affine is invariant under isomorphism and Zariski local on the base (conditions (0) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-local-on-base-criterion] for $\mathcal P$ = affine).* (0): let $f:X\to S$ be affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and $a:X\to\tilde X$, $b:S\to\tilde S$ isomorphisms of schemes with $\tilde f\circ a=b\circ f$. Let $W\subseteq\tilde S$ be an affine open. Then $V=b^{-1}(W)$ is an affine open of $S$ (the isomorphism $b$ restricts to an isomorphism of open subschemes $V\to W$ [def-pc-scheme]), so $f^{-1}(V)$ is affine; and $\tilde f^{-1}(W)=a(f^{-1}(b^{-1}(W)))=a(f^{-1}(V))$ because $\tilde f=b f a^{-1}$, and $a$ restricts to an isomorphism of open subschemes $f^{-1}(V)\to\tilde f^{-1}(W)$; hence $\tilde f^{-1}(W)$ is affine, and $\tilde f$ is affine. (2): let $S=\bigcup_kV_k$ be an open covering such that each restriction $f_k:f^{-1}(V_k)\to V_k$ is affine. Each open subscheme $V_k$ is covered by affine opens $W$ of $V_k$, which are affine opens of $S$ [def-pc-scheme]; for such $W$, $f^{-1}(W)=f_k^{-1}(W)$ is affine because $f_k$ is affine. These $W$ (over all $k$) form an affine open covering of $S$ whose preimages are affine, so $f$ is affine by [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] (third condition implies the first).

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L5 (lemma-descending-property-affine, line 5926), proof, second sentence: 'Being affine is Zariski local on the base, see Morphisms, Lemma 01S8' (morphisms-lemma-characterize-affine, morphisms.tex line 1736); invariance under isomorphism is the convention of Definition Tag 02KO (definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310)

proof.text: *Being affine is stable under base change (condition (1)).* If $f:X\to S$ is affine and $g:S'\to S$ is any morphism, in particular a flat one, then the second projection $X\times_SS'\to S'$ is affine by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L5 (lemma-descending-property-affine, line 5926), proof, first sentence: 'A base change of an affine morphism is affine, see Morphisms, Lemma 01SD' (morphisms-lemma-base-change-affine, morphisms.tex line 1982)

proof.text: *Condition (3): the setting.* Let $g:S'\to S$ be a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] morphism of affine schemes, $f:X\to S$ a morphism, $X'=X\times_SS'$ the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $g':X'\to X$, $f':X'\to S'$, and assume $f'$ affine. By step 1 (invariance under isomorphism, applied to $f$, $g$ and $f'$) we may assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ [def-pc-scheme], so $g=\operatorname{Spec}\rho$ for a unique ring map $\rho:R\to R'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. (a) $g$ is a morphism of affine schemes, hence affine [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], hence quasi-compact by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]; so $g$ is flat, surjective and quasi-compact. (b) $X'$ is affine by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] ($f'$ affine, $S'$ affine); write $A'=\Gamma(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$. (c) $f'$ is quasi-compact and separated by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. We have to show that $X$ is affine (then $f$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]); this is done in steps 4-6.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L5 (lemma-descending-property-affine, line 5926), proof, lines 5935-5940: 'let g : S' -> S be a flat surjective morphism of affine schemes, and let f : X -> S be a morphism. Assume that the base change f' : X' -> S' is affine. In other words, X' is affine, say X' = Spec(A'). Also write S = Spec(R) and S' = Spec(R'). We have to show that X is affine.'

proof.text: *$X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.* By step 3, $g$ is flat, surjective and quasi-compact and $f'$ is quasi-compact and separated. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-quasi-compact], $f$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-separated], $f$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $S$ is affine, the scheme $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L5 (lemma-descending-property-affine, line 5926), proof, lines 5943-5944: 'By Lemmas 02KQ and 02KU we see that X -> S is separated and quasi-compact.'

proof.text: *Flat base change of global sections.* Let $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, an $R$-algebra through $\alpha=f^\sharp:R\to A$ (the map on global sections, $R=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]). Since $g$ is flat, $S,S'$ are affine and $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (step 4), [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs] gives that $$\beta:A\otimes_RR'\to A'=\Gamma(X',\mathcal O_{X'}),\qquad a\otimes r'\mapsto g'^\sharp(a)\,f'^\sharp(r'),$$ is a ring isomorphism. (The source phrases this as $f_*\mathcal O_X=\widetilde A$ and $g^*f_*\mathcal O_X=f'_*\mathcal O_{X'}$ through Schemes, Lemma 01LC; on the affine bases $S,S'$ the statement on global sections is what the argument uses, so the quasi-coherence of $f_*\mathcal O_X$ is not needed.)

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L5 (lemma-descending-property-affine, line 5926), proof, lines 5945-5953: 'Thus f_*O_X is a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_S-algebras ... Hence f_*O_X = A~ for some R-algebra A. In fact A = Gamma(X, O_X) of course. Also, by flat base change (Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02KH) we have g^*f_*O_X = f'_*O_{X'}. In other words, we have A' = R' (x)_R A.'

proof.text: *The canonical morphism $c:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and its base change.* By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] there is a unique morphism $c:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $c^\sharp=\mathrm{id}_A$ on global sections, and for every ring $B$ the bijection $\operatorname{Mor}(Y,\operatorname{Spec}B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(B,\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y))$, $u\mapsto u^\sharp$, satisfies $(v\circ u)^\sharp=u^\sharp\circ v^\sharp$ (functoriality of global sections). (a) $f=\operatorname{Spec}\alpha\circ c$: both have global-sections map $\alpha$ (as $(\operatorname{Spec}\alpha)^\sharp=\alpha$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $c^\sharp=\mathrm{id}$), so they agree by the bijectivity. (b) Let $T=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RR')$ with $h=\operatorname{Spec}(a\mapsto a\otimes1):T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $q=\operatorname{Spec}(r'\mapsto1\otimes r'):T\to S'$; by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] $(T,h,q)$ is a fibre product of $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha$ and $g$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. (c) Let $c':X'\to T$ be the morphism with $c'^\sharp=\beta$ (step 5) [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Comparing global-sections maps: $(h\circ c')^\sharp=\beta\circ(a\mapsto a\otimes1)=g'^\sharp=(c\circ g')^\sharp$ and $(q\circ c')^\sharp=\beta\circ(r'\mapsto1\otimes r')=f'^\sharp$, so $h\circ c'=c\circ g'$ and $q\circ c'=f'$. (d) Consider the diagram with top row $g':X'\to X$, middle row $h:T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, bottom row $g:S'\to S$, and vertical maps $c':X'\to T$, $c:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, $q:T\to S'$, $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$; both squares commute by (c) and (b). The lower square is cartesian by (b), and the outer rectangle is $(X',g',q\circ c'=f')$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha\circ c=f$ and $g$, which is cartesian by the definition of $X'$ and (a). By [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the upper square is cartesian: $(X',g',c')$ is a fibre product of $c$ and $h$. (e) $c'$ is an isomorphism: $X'$ is affine (step 3(b)), say $e:\operatorname{Spec}B\to X'$ an isomorphism [def-pc-scheme]; then $c'\circ e=\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ for a unique $\psi:A\otimes_RR'\to B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and by the functoriality of global sections $\psi=e^\sharp\circ\beta$ (identifying $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B)=B$), a composite of ring isomorphisms; so $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ is an isomorphism (with inverse $\operatorname{Spec}\psi^{-1}$, by functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]), and $c'=\operatorname{Spec}\psi\circ e^{-1}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L5 (lemma-descending-property-affine, line 5926), proof, lines 5954-5959: 'Consider the canonical morphism X -> Spec(A) over S from Schemes, Lemma 01I1 (schemes-lemma-morphism-into-affine, schemes.tex line 841). By the above the base change of this morphism to S' is an isomorphism.'

proof.text: *Descent of the isomorphism, and condition (3).* The morphism $h:T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ of step 6 is the base change of $g$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha$ (step 6(b)); so $h$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], and quasi-compact because it is a morphism of affine schemes, hence affine [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and quasi-compact by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. By step 6(d),(e), $(X',g',c')$ is a fibre product of $c$ and $h$ whose projection $c':X'\to T$ is an isomorphism; by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-isomorphism] (with $\varphi=c$, $p=g'$, $\varphi'=c'$), $c:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an isomorphism. Hence $X$ is affine [def-pc-scheme], and $f:X\to S$, a morphism of affine schemes, is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Thus being affine satisfies condition (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-local-on-base-criterion].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L5 (lemma-descending-property-affine, line 5926), proof, lines 5959-5961: 'Hence it is an isomorphism by Lemma 02L4 (lemma-descending-property-isomorphism, line 5915).' (The morphism Spec(A') -> Spec(A) along which 02L4 is applied is the base change of S' -> S, hence flat, surjective, and quasi-compact as a morphism of affine schemes.)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 1, 2 and 7 the class of affine morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism] satisfies conditions (0)-(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-local-on-base-criterion]. Applied to $f:X\to S$ and the fpqc covering $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], whose base changes $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ are affine by hypothesis, it gives that $f$ is affine.
